seoTitle: Free Hreflang Tag Generator for Multilingual Sites
metaDescription: Turn language and URL pairs into hreflang link tags and sitemap xhtml:link markup, with checks for codes and x-default. Free, in-browser.
intro: Enter one language code and URL per line to generate hreflang link tags for the page head and the equivalent xhtml:link entries for a sitemap, with warnings for invalid codes.
why:
Hreflang tells search engines which language or regional version of a page to show to which visitors. It is easy to get wrong: codes must be valid, every URL must be absolute, each version must list all the others and itself, and a fallback x-default is recommended.

This generator takes lines such as en-GB | https://example.com/uk/ and prints the link tags to paste in the head of every version, plus the same set as xhtml:link elements for an XML sitemap. It reports invalid codes, relative URLs and duplicate codes, and reminds you when there is no x-default. It does not check that your pages actually link to each other. For that, use the hreflang validator. The generation is done in your browser.
howTo: Enter one pair per line in the form code | URL, for example nl-BE | https://example.com/nl-be/.
Add an x-default line for the fallback page.
Run the tool and fix any errors it lists.
Paste the full set of tags into the head of every language version, or use the sitemap markup instead.

faq.a: Use ISO 639-1 language codes, optionally followed by an ISO 3166-1 region such as en-GB or nl-BE. The tool flags invalid combinations. x-default is the special value for unmatched users.

faq.q: Do I need the tags on every page version?
faq.a: Yes. Each version must list all alternates, including itself, and the links must be reciprocal. Missing return links are a common reason hreflang is ignored.

faq.q: Head tags or sitemap, which should I use?
faq.a: Either works, and you should not need both. Head tags suit small sites. A sitemap is easier to maintain on large sites, since the markup is in one file.
